opening.argument: The description presents an “Automated trading system giveaway” and immediately supplies an external LINE link. That pairing gives viewers a concrete route to pursue an unusually easy reward: follow the external link to obtain the offered system. The material therefore contains more than general cryptocurrency discussion; it connects a giveaway claim with a viewer action and directs attention outside the video. The absence of a stated deposit does not remove the solicitation, because the promised item is framed as free and the access route is the linked contact channel.

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling the video an investigation does not explain away the separate promotional description. The title's question and the speaker's doubts concern the wallet, but the description still offers an automated trading system and supplies a direct external contact route. The defense identifies no limitation stating that the giveaway is merely hypothetical or unavailable.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The description does not state that clicking the link yields a reward, nor does it specify registration, verification, payment, or delivery. “Giveaway” and an external URL establish promotion, but they do not establish the required consequential acquisition flow. The spoken material instead repeatedly discusses uncertainty and risk, so the link alone cannot convert the whole video into a low-barrier reward scam.

opening.argument: The central financial proposition has the hallmark of passive investment returns: Hite Wallet is described as holding Ethereum-based tokens, with expected capital and income gains, and a monthly interest rate of about 10%. That is not ordinary market commentary; it links participation in a wallet to a recurring, unusually high return. The broader discussion reinforces the same high-return framing by describing 30% or 60% monthly returns as a familiar standard and mentioning returns of 100 or 200 times. Even with warnings, repeating these figures can make the opportunity appear credible and attractive while leaving the underlying mechanism unverified.

citations.quote: Hite wallet is a wallet that can store ethereum-based tokens. The price is expected to rise in terms of capital gain and income gain. Moreover, the interest rate is very high. The monthly interest rate is about 10%.
The monthly basis was 30% or 60% and it was the standard.
This time, it was 100 times or 200 times.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense treats the warning language as dispositive, but the financial pitch remains unusually specific: a wallet, expected gains, and approximately 10% monthly interest. Saying that high-return products are dangerous can also function as credibility-building candor, especially when the same presentation supplies multiple large-return figures. The alleged withdrawal and hacking problems do not establish that the underlying offer was safe or legitimate.

The speaker expressly says, “There is no product that returns high with low risk,” and describes the situation as uncertain. A high rate may be evidence of risk or dubious economics, but it does not by itself establish deceptive investment solicitation or a promised return.

opening.argument: Although presented as news, the video repeatedly gives the wallet and token an appreciation-and-income frame. Hite Wallet is associated with expected capital gain and income gain, while the title brands PlusToken as a “Dividend Wallet.” The closing also says viewers may choose to purchase or buy in the future, and the description advertises “skyrocketing coin updates.” Taken together, the news format can operate as promotional positioning: discuss the controversy, emphasize possible upside, and leave viewers with a path toward buying a token-related product. The warning tone does not eliminate the promotional effect of repeatedly foregrounding appreciation, dividends, and future purchase.

The price is expected to rise in terms of capital gain and income gain.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense's investigation framing does not negate the promotional signals surrounding the product. The title uses “Dividend Wallet,” the description promises “skyrocketing” updates, and the closing mentions future purchase. Those are not necessary to explain a neutral investigation and can steer viewers toward token participation even while the speaker acknowledges controversy.

skyrocketing coin updates

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The title is phrased as a collapse question, not a purchase instruction, and “skyrocketing coin updates” is promotional wording in the description without a specified token-buying procedure. The closing only says viewers may choose to purchase or buy in the future; it does not identify what to buy, where to buy it, or require participation. The evidence therefore supports discussion of token claims, not a demonstrated purchase solicitation.
